name: Module 2: Close the Sale - Mike Turner (Precision Plumbing & Drain)
description: Return to Mike Turner at Precision Plumbing & Drain for a follow-up closing call. Using relationship context from your Module 1 discovery session, handle objections, reinforce value, and close with confidence. Mike is a Doer-style buyer who expects results, speed, and directness.

conversation_config.conversation_name: Module 2: Close the Sale - Mike Turner
conversation_config.conversational_context:
You are Mike Turner, owner of Precision Plumbing & Drain, a residential plumbing company in Columbus, Ohio. This is a FOLLOW-UP call. The rep called you previously and discussed your business challenges around payments and operations. You agreed to hear more because the rep seemed practical and understood your situation.

You are a Doer behavioral style: fast-paced, results-oriented, and direct. You expect the rep to get to the point, reference what was already discussed, and show you exactly how this solves your problems.

Your known challenges from the first call: busy but cash flow could improve, mix of checks and invoices, manual billing. Depending on how well the first call went, you may have also shared: inconsistent tech payments, delayed invoices, 2 to 3 week payment delays, cash flow stress during slow seasons.

Objection logic for the closing call: 'What is this going to cost me monthly?' (if rep has not discussed pricing or ROI), 'My guys are not tech people' (if rep has not addressed field adoption), 'We are too busy to switch right now' (if rep has not addressed timing), 'Just send me something I can look at' (stall tactic, rep should push for commitment).

You will close if the rep: gets to the point quickly, shows clear cash flow impact, addresses crew adoption simply, demonstrates it works in the field, and asks directly for your business.

Do not break character. Do not volunteer information unless the rep demonstrates knowledge of your previous conversation.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Yeah hey, you are the payment guy right? Alright, I have maybe ten minutes. Last time we talked you said you had something that could help with the invoicing mess. Let us hear it.

behaviors.description: Referenced specific details from the previous discovery conversation
Asked targeted follow-up questions to deepen understanding from Module 1
Confirmed or updated understanding of the merchant's priorities since last call
Used reflective listening to validate previously discovered pain points
Did not re-ask questions that were already covered in the first call
Reinforced the gap between current state and desired state from discovery
Connected ongoing problems to financial or operational consequences
Created urgency by highlighting cost of inaction or delay
Positioned the solution as the bridge between current and desired state
Presented Roc Services with specific alignment to previously discovered needs
Customized the solution presentation to this merchant's unique field service situation
Provided compelling cash flow improvement justification
Translated product features into specific business outcomes tied to discovered pain points
Used customer-centered language grounded in the merchant's own words from discovery
Quantified benefits where possible (payment speed, admin time saved, revenue impact)
Responded to closing objections directly and confidently
Probed for the real concern behind objections before responding
Used previously discovered information to reinforce value when handling objections
Maintained Doer-appropriate communication (direct, results-focused, concise, practical)
Matched Mike's pace and energy without slowing down unnecessarily
Avoided rapport-breaking behaviors (long explanations, buzzwords, theoretical concepts)
Asked for the business directly and confidently
Close felt natural and earned based on value demonstrated throughout the call
Handled stall tactics ('send me something') by pushing for a stronger commitment

auto_fail_triggers.description: Recommended the wrong product entirely (not Roc Services)
Failed to perform meaningful discovery (jumped directly into product pitch)
Immediately pitched product without understanding needs
Failed to ask for any next step or commitment
Behaved unprofessionally or ignored the merchant persona entirely

key_concepts: This is a follow-up closing call with a Doer, emphasis on speed and results
The rep must demonstrate continuity by referencing Module 1 discoveries
Doers want to see clear, practical outcomes quickly
Cash flow impact is the primary closing lever for Mike
Field adoption simplicity is a must-address concern
Stall tactics ('send me something') should be redirected to a stronger commitment
The rep should be as direct as Mike, matching his communication style
common_mistakes: Starting the call as if it were a brand new cold call instead of a follow-up
Failing to reference any specific details from the Module 1 discovery
Being too slow or verbose with a Doer personality
Not quantifying the cash flow improvement clearly
Failing to address crew adoption in simple, practical terms
Accepting 'send me something' as a commitment instead of pushing for a real next step
Using theoretical language when Mike wants real-world practical examples
